note: Who owns every field in a Tranche 1 packet. A field owned by the court, the clerk, the prosecuting authority or a notary is left blank on the generated document — LegalEase never completes another actor's block. A field owned by the participant is either filled from their answer or printed as a rule for them to complete by hand.

common.appearsIn: caption, allegations, prayer, signature block, certificate

common.ifAbsent: the clause is omitted; no blank rule is printed

common.appearsIn: petitioner's statement section, reproduced verbatim and labelled as theirs

ms-misd-addl.appearsIn: selects the statutory citation and sentence
ms-misd-addl.ifAbsent: generation stops; an unapproved value fails closed

ms-nonconv.ifAbsent: generation stops; an unapproved value fails closed
a blank rule is printed; the no-charge-filed branch does not use it

leftBlank.why: Signed by hand after the participant has read and checked the petition. LegalEase never signs for anyone.
Dated when signed, not when generated.

leftBlank.field: Judge signature and date on the proposed order
leftBlank.why: The court signs its own order. No signature rule is even drawn for the participant on an order.

leftBlank.field: Grant and deny checkboxes on the proposed order
leftBlank.why: The outcome is the court's decision. Both boxes render blank.
Completed when the copy is actually delivered.

leftBlank.field: Date on the § 99-19-71(2)(b) district attorney notice
leftBlank.why: Completed when the notice is delivered, because the ten days run from receipt.
Supplied by the clerk after filing. It is a manual-completion item, not a generation input.
Unresolved for these routes. No amount is printed and the participant is told to ask.
Never asserted. The packet does not represent that the prosecutor agrees.
The petitions carry a truth statement rather than a notarized verification. Whether any district requires one is an open question for counsel.
